MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 23, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Ury at 5:01 p.m., on February 23, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 18, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum (arrived at 5:05 p.m.)
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager /Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel and Director of Public Services (Animal Shelter);
  Threat to Public Services or Facilities Pursuant to paragraph (e) of Section 54954.5.

CS2. Conference With Legal Counsel: Consideration of Initiation of Litigation Pursuant
  to Paragraph (4) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: One Case; Adverse to State of
  California.

City Council Minutes  1  February 23, 2016
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02, Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was nothing to report from Closed Session.

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Raths

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Simone Kvalhein, M.V.: stated that she is building a merchant processing business in Mission
Viejo and she asked the City to help her in creating more veterans-centric businesses. She offered
to provide business grants for ten veterans and she asked the City to help connect her with veterans
who may benefit.

Jim Leach, Santa Margarita Water District: discussed the new rate structure at the Santa Water
District and notified the community that there has been a disruption in the billing system which
delayed the February customer bills. He noted that the District is working diligently to make sure
that the rate structure is implemented accurately and while they regret the disruption and potential
confusion, they are making every effort to send accurate bills.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 3, 4, 16, and 17 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.
City Council Minutes  2  February 23, 2016
 4.  Check Register Dated February 5, 2016 in the Amount of $808,821.82

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Quarterly Check Register Reports - Second Quarter of FY 2015-16

  Received and filed.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for December 2015

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for December 2015

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  December 2015

  Received and filed.

9.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for December 2015

  Received and filed.

10.  Quarterly Financial Report - Second Quarter of FY 2015-16

  Received and filed.

11.  Semi-Annual Financial Report for the Mission Viejo Community Development
  Financing Authority for the Six Months Ended December 31, 2015

  Received and filed.

12.  Claim Against the City - Scott Holcomb

  Rejected claim.
City Council Minutes  3  February 23, 2016
 13.  800 MHz Next Generation Radio Equipment Purchase

  Approved a purchase order to Motorola Solutions, Inc. in the amount of $292,334.13 for
  the purchase of radios for the 800 MHz Next Generation Countywide Coordinated
  Communication System (CCCS).

15.  Acceptance of Tract Map 17392 and Associated Bonds and Agreements

  (1) Approved Final Tract Map 17392 and authorized the City Clerk and the City Engineer
  to sign the record map subject to any minor revisions required by the City Engineer; (2)
  authorized the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign the Subdivision Improvement Agreement
  with CalAtlantic Group, Inc. (formerly Standard Pacific Homes) for Tract Map 17392
  subject to any minor revisions required by the City Attorney; and (3) accepted the
  associated Subdivision Faithful Performance Bonds, Subdivision Labor and Materials
  Bonds, Subdivision Monument Bond, Landscape Bond, and all associated Riders, as
  described in the Subdivision Improvement Agreement.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she was absent at the last meeting but because
  she watched the video, she is qualified to vote on approval of the Minutes.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve the
  Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of February 9, 2016, as presented.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

3.  Check Register Dated January 29, 2016 in the Amount of $539,250.17

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about a payment made for office locks within city hall.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that staff has
  been working on projects over the last few years to harden city hall and create more safe
  zones.

City Council Minutes  4  February 23, 2016
   Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

14.  2016 Pavement Management Program Update

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern that the cost of the updates varies from year
  to year.

  Director Chagnon responded that most of the Pavement Management Program updates are
  minor in nature but every six years a major update is required. That increased time and
  effort results in higher costs.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to authorize staff to
  issue a purchase order to Nichols Consulting Engineers, Chtd., for the update of the City's
  Pavement Management Program in an amount not to exceed $51,300.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

16.  Alicia Parkway Traffic Signal Synchronization Project (Project P) Cooperative
  Agreement

  Council Member Schlicht asked when the traffic signals on Alicia Parkway were last
  synchronized and she expressed concern with increased delays for cross traffic at
  intersections.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to ratify to approve
  Cooperative Agreement No. C-5-3586 with the Orange County Transportation Authority
  (OCTA) for the Alicia Parkway Traffic Signal Synchronization Project (CIP 227).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  5  February 23, 2016
   AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

17.  Project V Local Transit Grant Applications

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report and answered the
  Council Members questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 16-04 Approving the Submittal of a Local Transit Improvement Project
  to the Orange County Transportation Authority for Funding Under Project V Community-
  Based Transit/Circulators; (2) adopt Resolution 16-05 Approving the Submittal of Two
  Local Transit Planning Projects to the Orange County Transportation Authority for
  Funding Under Project V Community-Based Transit/Circulators.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  Council Member Schlicht noted for the record that she could not vote yes because she
  doesn't believe that the Council has enough information to make a sound decision based
  on a survey for 2008.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

18.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

19.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

20.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Mayor Ury presented the report.

City Council Minutes  6  February 23, 2016
 STAFF REPORTS

21.  Status of Development Projects in Mission Viejo

  City Manager Wilberg provided an update on the major development projects that are
  underway in the City, including Skyridge residential development, NCA medical office
  building, the Hampton Inn & Suites, Greenstreet project and Orchard Hardware.

22.  Senate Bill No. 876 Relating to Homelessness and Public Spaces

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Ury, to take the position to
  oppose SB 876 and direct the City Manager to send a letter to the legislature.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

23.  Assembly Bill No. 1666 Community Facilities Districts: Reports

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Sharon Campbell, M.V.: speaking on behalf of Assemblyman Bill Brough, she asked the
  City Council to support the proposed bill.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to
  take the position to support AB 1666 and direct the City Manager to send a letter to the
  legislature.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

24.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

City Council Minutes  7  February 23, 2016
   By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths announced that he had nothing to report.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs discussed the issue of sober living homes in the County and the State and
what municipalities can and cannot do. He stated that these homes are growing in number and
becoming a problem to neighbors. Sober living homes can cause property values to go down and
some people are moving to get away from them. Council Member Sachs discussed the history of
the issue which began in 1998 and subsequently there have been 35 pieces of legislation to try and
control sober living homes. The most devastating legislation established that up to 6 residents can
live in the homes but what is not regulated are the necessary controls that would allow cities to
manage them. Council Member Sachs said sober living homes are becoming more prevalent and
it is an area that he is particularly interested in so he will conduct a town hall meeting on the topic
sometime in April, 2016. He plans to invite experts to discuss the issues and teach residents what
can be done to protect themselves and their property values.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that a number of years ago, Mission Viejo residents were
defrauded by the California Public Utilities Commission over the Viejo Systems Project and she
expressed her concern with Electro Magnetic Fields (EMF.) She said that kids are being pulled
out of school in San Diego because parents are concerned about high EMF and now, an
Administrative Law Judge has written an article stating that the CPUC is biased. Coincidentally,
resident Joe Holtzman recently tested Mission Viejo’s Flo Jo Park and he reported that EMF levels
were off the charts. Council Member Schlicht noted that Mission Viejo used to have EMF warning
signs and she recommended that those signs be reinstated, especially in parks. She asked Mayor
Pro Tem Bucknum when she is available for another ad hoc meeting on the PACE program and
shared her continued concerns with PACE. She said that even the office of the Treasurer-Tax
Collector has concerns about PACE products and has put together a pamphlet with an overview of
the programs. Council Member Schlicht asked if there will be a mitigated negative declaration
with the planned swim and dive center renovations and she stated that the new aquatics complex
is expected to revive the area and traffic and attendance should be in harmony with the
neighborhood. Council Member Schlicht inquired about browning grass at the dog park and she
raised her concern with AB 1732, a bill that would mandate coed bathrooms for private businesses
including churches and public buildings. She stated that the City should consider unisex doors for
the new bathrooms at Pavion Park. She also shared her concern with the closing of El Toro RV
storage because there are not enough storage units that are affordable for residents of South

City Council Minutes  8  February 23, 2016
 County. Council Member Schlicht stated that the City needs to reevaluate its RV rules because
they are interfering with commerce. She also said she has continued concerns with visibility of
the traffic light as one is driving south on Muirlands approaching Marathon. Council Member
Schlicht asked Mayor Ury to adjourn the meeting in honor of Judge Scalia and she read a quote
from him: “I believe that judges should adhere to the text of the law and not amend or revise it to
accord with what they think the law ought to be.”

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum discussed her attendance at recent events including the City’s volunteer
recognition luncheon, the Chamber of Commerce mixer at Ballpark Pizza, the Orange County
Government Leaders Prayer Breakfast, the grand opening celebration for the Mission Viejo Bocce
Ball courts, and girls softball opening day. She stated that she is also looking forward the baseball
little league grand openings next weekend. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum announced that the City’s
recreation centers have some new programs and she encouraged residents to look into the Parents
Date Night childcare event on Friday March 11 at the Marguertie Tennis Pavilion. Parents can go
out from 5:00 to 9:00 p.m. and the cost is $20 per child. There is also a group exercise class called
TRX among other new events at the recreation centers. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum thanked Senator
Patricia Bates for hosting the South Orange County Senior Day with Assemblyman Bill Brough
on March 11 from 8 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center. And in closing, she
announced that the City’s 2015 Annual Report is now available and she encouraged residents to
pick up a copy.

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury thanked his colleagues for filling in for him when he was sick the past couple of
weeks. He said he did however attend the softball opening day which was a lot of fun as was the
Bocce Ball Park grand opening. Mayor Ury noted that Mission Viejo does everything first class
and the bocce ball courts look great. Resident Anna T. Boyce threw out the first ball and he said
he knows that the courts will be well used. He also attended the Orange County Business Council
annual dinner where the new Board President and Board Members were seated. Mayor Ury
announced that the Rotary Club will hold its annual Texas Hold ‘Em tournament on June 11 this
year and proceeds will go to a local charity of the player’s choice.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:23 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in memory of Supreme Court Justice Antonin Scalia, to
Tuesday, March 8, 2016, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of March 8, 2016
City Council Minutes  9  February 23, 2016
